Meeting header: 2026-05-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Leo Martinez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Helio Head of Platform), Tom Reynolds (Helio SRE), Miguel Alvarez (Helio CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Redwood and Helio discussed Dedicated POC capacity ramp, autoscale policies, burst handling, and next steps for a canary rollout. Action items assigned for pricing, stress tests, SAML/KMS details and traffic artifacts.

Topics: dedicated sizing, autoscale policy tuning, burst credits/eviction, KV cache sizing, fallback routing, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), rollout timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. quick round of intros?
[00:05] Aisha: hi, aisha here, i own platform at helio, running the payments infra, excited to get the dedicated pilot stable for peak season.
[00:12] Tom: tom, sre, i mostly worry about tail latency and thundering herd.
[00:16] Miguel: miguel, cto, will join for architecture decisions today.
[00:20] Leo: leo from redwood, i'll do the deep dive on autoscale and KV cache behavior.
[00:24] Samira: cool, agenda: quick results readout from last week's tests, tuning items, burst planning, security checklist, then next steps.

[00:37] Aisha: quick note, we ran the 2-hour baseline yesterday using the sample traffic you gave, saw p50 ~80ms p95 ~210ms and p99 spiked to 1.4s, which triggered our alert.
[00:47] Leo: okay got it, was that with the cache warmed? were you using persistent KV cache?
[00:52] Tom: it was mostly cold starts, we restarted the pool between tests to emulate redeploys.
[00:55] Leo: right that will blow up p99, dedicated has pre-warm options and we can suggest an eviction policy.

[01:05] Samira: let's talk autoscale policy — currently you're on reactive scale with min 2 gpus and max 12, burst credits set to 1000 token-equivalents. are those numbers still accurate?
[01:16] Aisha: yes min 2 max 12, we picked those from the sizing doc you shared but we're flexible if you recommend changes.
[01:22] Leo: from the telemetry, your average concurrency needs 4 pods during business hours and spikes to ~9 for payment window bursts. I'd recommend min 3, target scale 6 with aggressive burst policy: short-lived extra nodes up to 12 that decay after 10 minutes unless sustained. that reduces cold start churn.
[01:39] Miguel: how does decay work? if a burst lifts usage to 12 then drops, do we have eviction that doesn't kill in-progress sessions?
[01:44] Leo: yes the runtime drains replicas, existing KV caches are rehydrated, we also recommend graceful connection draining to avoid 20-30% token loss from aborted requests. there is slight increased cost but better latency stability.

[01:56] Tom: question on cache: what's the recommended KV cache size for our median sequence length — our median prompt is 420 tokens, but top-10 prompts go to 2k tokens.
[02:05] Leo: we'll run a sizing sim — but initial rule: keep KV warm for top-n users and use an LRU policy. for long sequences, we suggest prefix caching for repeated system context. I'll run a sim to show hit-rate vs memory tradeoff.

[02:20] Aisha: okay, on the burst credits model we worry about cost — can you recap how burst credits charge vs reserved capacity?
[02:27] Samira: sure. reserved capacity is fixed monthly; burst credits are metered usage above reserved capacity billed per-token. we also offer transient 'pre-warm' credits to mitigate p99 without paying for always-on headroom. we'll share the pricing worksheet after this call.

[02:40] Miguel: any way to trade latency for cost at runtime — like degrade to smaller quantized model for non-sensitive requests?
[02:46] Leo: yes, policy-based routing can send non-PII requests to a cheaper quantized variant or to an embeddings-only path. Redwood supports model-variant fallback and A/B routing. you can specify selectors like "non-financial, low-precision" to route.

[02:59] Tom: are there risk of consistency issues when we fall back? e.g. session KV mismatch between variants?
[03:05] Leo: good point. for now we sync KV at request boundaries and recommend per-request binding to model-variant. rare edge cases exist, we'll add a note to the playbook: avoid mixing variants mid-session for critical flows.

[03:18] Aisha: security checklist: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, kkm— i mean kms, and audit logs retained for 12 months. are those supported in dedicated?
[03:25] Samira: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering, SAML/SSO, customer-managed KMS keys, and extended audit logs (add-on). we'll send SOC2 artifact link after the call.

[03:36] Miguel: latency SLOs — our success criteria is p99 < 200ms for auth and high-value txn flows. feasible?
[03:43] Leo: with warmed caches and the autoscale tweaks i mentioned, p99 < 200ms is achievable for the 80th percentile of traffic. for sustained peak we may need more reserved capacity or pre-warm credits.

[03:54] Tom: can we do a controlled 10x blast to validate fallback and scale?
[03:58] Samira: yes, we propose a 4-hour stress test at 10x baseline during off-peak, Redwood will run and share logs + perf matrix.

[04:06] Aisha: timing?
[04:08] Samira: target this Saturday 02:00 UTC unless you prefer weekday.
[04:11] Tom: weekend is better. we'll provide keys and traffic generator.

[04:20] Leo: technical note — our autoscaler uses combination of CPU/gpu token backpressure and request queue length. you can tune the alarm thresholds: queue depth threshold, scale-up cooldown, scale-down decay. for billing we send token usage by model-variant.

[04:36] Miguel: what's the cooldown you recommend? we saw oscillation in yesterday's test.
[04:40] Leo: set scale-up cooldown to 30s, scale-down decay to 600s for bursty workloads. also use hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping.

[04:51] Tom: we had an issue where routing fell back to hosted model in another region during outage, is there a way to pin region or enforce strict local-only fallback?
[04:59] Samira: yes you can configure region affinity and strict fallback policies. for regulated traffic we recommend strict-local with canary fallback to a pre-approved variant.

[05:10] Aisha: about observability, we need token-level breakdown and per-route p95/p99 traces. do you expose that?
[05:16] Leo: Redwood Console provides per-route, per-model metrics and tracing hooks you can pipe into your Datadog or Splunk. we'll give you a dashboard link and a CSV export from the stress test.

[05:25] Miguel: legal/procurement check — how long does it take to spin up dedicated in prod after we sign?
[05:30] Samira: typically 4-6 weeks for region provisioning and enterprise onboarding, 2-3 weeks if using our existing regions with reserved capacity.

[05:36] Tom: one more ops question: do you support node pinning or taints for noisy neighbors?
[05:40] Leo: yes, Dedicated exposes node pools and labels. you can taint a pool for latency-sensitive models. also support isolated NVMe for KV cache hot storage.

[05:48] Aisha: let's recap canary plan: schedule a small traffic slice to the dedicated pool, monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate for 2 hours, if stable promote.
[05:56] Samira: exactly. we'll prepare a runbook: pre-checks, smoke tests, rollback criteria.

[06:02] Miguel: curious about fallback behavior, what happens if dedicated pool hits quota? will we get an explicit 429 or automatic degrade?
[06:09] Leo: depends on policy. options: 1) queue until capacity frees 2) return 429 immediately 3) route to fallback model variant. you configure per-route fallback. for payment flows we recommend queue+notify then fail closed if queue > threshold.

[06:23] Tom: slightly worried about KV eviction during scale-down. any recommendations?
[06:28] Leo: set sticky cache affinity for top sessions and extend TTLs during known windows. we can also orchestrate warmers to prefetch top keys on scale-up.

[06:37] Aisha: sounds good. can you put the warmers in the playbook?
[06:40] Samira: will do.

[06:42] Samira: ok let's do a quick recap and owners — Samira will share pricing worksheet and canary runbook; Leo will run KV sizing sim and provide autoscale parameter recommendations; Tom will upload SAML metadata and KMS alias; Aisha will confirm success criteria and upload traffic artifacts.

[06:55] Miguel: timeline to next sync?
[06:57] Samira: next sync after the stress test, propose Tue 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC to review results and finalize canary.

[07:05] Aisha: works for us. thanks.
[07:08] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links: pricing worksheet, SOC2 artifact, stress test runbook and dashboard link. end.
